title: Senior Optical Design Engineer
description: Ready to make connectivity from space universally accessible, secure and actionable? Then you’ve come to the right place! E-Space is bridging Earth and space to enable hyper-scaled deployments of Internet of Things (IoT) solutions and services. We are building a highly-advanced low Earth orbit (LEO) space system that will fundamentally change the design, economics, manufacturing and service delivery associated with traditional satellite and terrestrial IoT systems. We’re intentional, we’re unapologetically curious and we’re 100% committed to innovate space-based communications and deliver actionable intelligence that will expand global economies, protect space and our planet and enhance our overall quality of life. Overview We are expanding our optomechanical capabilities, and the success of our projects depends on optical designs that are precise, manufacturable, and verified through rigorous analysis and testing. As a Senior Optical Design Engineer, you will own optical designs from concept through lab validation, turning requirements into lens designs and optical assemblies that perform reliably in the real world. This position is central to our mission of delivering cutting-edge free-space optical systems for space applications, and it will support successful pre-production runs and strong collaboration with our suppliers. This position reports to our Responsible Engineer, Optical Systems, and is based in our Toulouse, France office. Our working language is English. What you will be doing Design and optimize lenses and optical systems, from first-order layout to detailed optimization with ray tracing and physical optics propagation (POP). Carry out tolerance analysis and Monte Carlo simulations to predict manufacturing and assembly yield, and define realistic tolerances with suppliers. Conduct STOP (Structural-Thermal-Optical Performance) analysis with mechanical engineers, verifying performance and margins across operating conditions. Conduct stray light analysis. Produce lens and optomechanical drawings, and work with mechanical engineers to ensure designs are manufacturable and assemblable. Define assembly, alignment, and bonding procedures, and support their implementation in clean room environments. Plan and execute lab assembly and test, covering alignment, characterization, and performance verification of prototypes and flight-representative hardware. Characterize components and assemblies through optical metrology, and identify discrepancies . D rive root-cause investigations and design iterations. Work with suppliers on design for manufacturing, tolerancing, inspection, qualification, and pre-production runs. What you bring to this role A Master’s degree in Optical Engineering, Physics, or a related field, with a strong foundation in geometrical and physical optics. 5+ years of experience in optical design, including lens and optical system design , optimization and STOP analysis. Proficiency in Zemax OpticStudio, including sequential ray tracing and optimization. Hands-on lab experience in optical assembly and test, with working knowledge of metrology instruments such as interferometers, wavefront sensors, MTF benches, autocollimators, and centration measurement tools. Experience with spaceborne optics or qualification to space-relevant standards, such as ECSS. Selection of adhesives, coatings and optics materials. Strong analytical skills and the ability to troubleshoot problems across simulation and hardware. A proactive mindset and a commitment to high standards of quality and performance. Bonus points Experience with free space optical communication systems . Python and ZOS-API skills for automating analysis or processing data. Experience with ANOVA methodology, including Gauge R&R studies and statistical post-processing in tools such as JMP. Practical knowledge of cleanroom practice, optics cleaning, adhesive bonding .
